rows.note: The page allows 2 to 4 credits for this course, so no credit figure is set.

rows.label: Three 3000+ technical electives (computer science courses)
rows.note: Only computer science courses are counted automatically, since the page makes every one of them eligible. Courses from other departments, and one 2000-level course, qualify only through a prerequisite check; see the confirm row.

rows.label: Check technical electives from other departments or at the 2000 level: confirm a qualifying prerequisite
rows.note: A technical elective outside computer science needs a qualifying prerequisite or corequisite listed in the course's catalog entry that term. One 2000-level course is allowed. Research courses may count, at most two, taken for a letter grade and worth 3 or more credits; research offered by other departments also needs faculty sign-off on its prerequisites.

rows.label: External specialization: three 3000+ courses outside computer science
rows.note: The board cannot see a shared prefix or an approved topic, nor tell which courses fall into the excluded types; the confirm row covers that.

limits.label: At most one course cross-listed with computer science

rows.label: Check the external specialization shares a prefix or approved topic and has no excluded course types
rows.note: The three courses must share a department prefix or a topic approved by a CS advisor. Courses of types such as research, independent study, team projects, PE or teaching assistant credit are not accepted.

rows.label: Major-approved elective: one course of 3+ credits or several totalling 3+ (letter grade or S/U, no AP/IB)
rows.note: Needs approval for the major; one course of 3+ credits or several totalling 3+. S/U grading is allowed (must earn S); AP/IB credit is not.

rows.label: Meet the declaration standards: C or better in CS and math, GPA floors (2.5 intro, 2.3 math), Cornell math if only test credit, good standing
rows.note: C or better in all CS and math courses; 2.5 average over intro CS and discrete math (or ECE 2400/ENGRD 2140, CS 2800/2802, CS 3110); 2.3 in calculus and critical math; Cornell letter grades. Only CS 3110 and CS 3410/3420 may supplement the CS GPA. If only AP or CASE credit shows for critical math, take another such course at Cornell. Second-major or switching students need good standing in their primary major. Confirm yourself.

rows.label: Major courses: letter grades, C- minimum, 2.5 GPA; PE, ROTC under 3000 and courses under 1100 do not count
rows.note: Major courses are letter-graded (except the approved elective) with a C- or higher; good standing also needs a 2.5 GPA in major courses. Physical education, ROTC courses under the 3000 level and courses under the 1100 level do not count toward the major.

rows.label: Three core courses finished before senior year
rows.note: Part of good standing for majors; checked by you or an advisor.

rows.label: Good standing each semester: credit load, term GPA, no failing grades
rows.note: At the end of every semester you need a full enough credit load, a term GPA of at least 2.3, and no failing grades (F, U or UX). The major-course GPA and grade floor are covered by the grades row. These are per-term conditions the board cannot check; confirm them yourself.
